notes: All definitions and examples were drastically shortened to roughly half the original length while preserving core meaning.

codes.name: access barriers
codes.definition: Structural obstacles to getting care, like distance or transport issues.
codes.negative_clarification: Not cost concerns — that's a separate issue.

positive_examples.text: Nearest clinic is 2 bus transfers away and can't get there without a full day off work.
positive_examples.why: Distance and transport physically block reaching care.

negative_examples.text: Doctor's copay was more than I could afford.

codes.name: cost concerns
codes.definition: Worry about the cost of care — bills, copays, or fear of debt.
codes.negative_clarification: Not difficulty reaching care (that's access barriers).

positive_examples.text: Skipped follow-up because couldn't afford $200 visit.
positive_examples.why: Care was forgone due to price.

negative_examples.text: Couldn't get an appointment for 3 months.
negative_examples.why: This is a scheduling delay, not about money.

codes.name: provider trust
codes.definition: Patient's confidence in or distrust of their clinician or health system.
codes.negative_clarification: Not general satisfaction with logistics like cost or wait times.

positive_examples.text: Doctor never listens, so I ignore the advice given.

negative_examples.text: Waiting room was crowded and I sat for an hour.
negative_examples.why: A logistics complaint, not about trust in the provider.

codes.name: wait times
codes.definition: Delay between seeking care and receiving it — appointment lead time or in-clinic wait.
codes.negative_clarification: Not being unable to reach the clinic (that's access barriers).

positive_examples.text: First available appointment was 4 months out.

negative_examples.text: No specialist within a hundred miles.
negative_examples.why: Care is unreachable, an access barrier, not just delayed.
